analysis:
The changes are documentation only, in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (new 'Deadline admission rates' section at head lines 523-548, code-map row at line 602) and docs/architecture/inference.md (out-of-order performance-observation freshness note around line 872, estimator-correction text around lines 1122-1158, deadline code-map row at line 2073). No executable code, keys, attestation, wire protocol, authorization or encryption paths are modified. Unit 9bceb6d953b336e2:0 is metadata only.

The docs describe provider-local TTFT/deadline admission estimators (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES, CBv2DecodeRateShape, IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate). They state that these shape time admission only. They say memory admission (slot and process byte admission, KV grants, activation floors) and the capacity wire fields are unchanged. If that holds, TB-002 and TB-007 availability assumptions (T-010, T-029) are not weakened. The code behind these claims is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm the described behavior. A later pass should check the AdmissionRateEstimators.swift change, because a mispriced deadline estimator could admit overload or reject legitimate work. It is availability- and quality-relevant, not confidentiality-relevant.

The docs state that heartbeat snapshots never renew evidence and that stale evidence older than 30 minutes is treated as absent. Those statements are consistent with the existing fail-closed posture. No change to the T-041 prefix-cache posture (30-minute TTL, HMAC lookup tags, account-scoped salt) appears in the supplied text. The 'decode charge' text mentions no change to the TTL.

No threat-model update is needed from these documentation-only changes. No concrete security regression was identified.
